newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Banacci downgraded by Finamex.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Banacci downgraded by Finamex.

text.p: Mexican brokerage Valores Finamex said Tuesday it downgraded Mexico's largest financial firm Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival (Banacci) to market performer from buy and lowered 1997 earnings per share estimates from 2.20 pesos to 0.60 pesos.

"This big downward revision in our 1997 estimate comes from a greater-than-expected impact from two factors: the application of the new accounting norms for Mexican banks and the change in Banamex's asset mix," analyst Rogelio Urrutia said in a report.

"At a price of 17.74 pesos per "B" share, Banacci trades at 29.1 times 1997 earnings and 15.1 times adjusted 1997 earnings (excluding change on monetary position of Banamex, its banking arm)," he added.

"We believe this valuation level fully reflects the competitive advantages of Banamex: its high-quality assets and its ability to resume lending at any time, which we expect to see this year," Urrutia said.

"By selling mortgage loans to Fobaproa (the government's bank insurance fund) in the Q4 of 1996, Banamex managed to decrease significantly the need to create more loan-less reserves in 1997. This will help to compensate for the 34 percent drop we expect to see in net interest income this year. The fall in interest income comes from the application of new accounting norms, which are stricter in recognizing delinquent loans," he added.

"In 1997, Banamex's total loans should increase 5 percent in real terms, in line with our estimates for GDP growth. Though this increase looks good at first sight, it will not be enough to make up for the fall in net interest income," he said.
